file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## linear-server

1	# Engineering Context — discourse-graph
2	
3	What you need to know to do good work in this codebase: how the team thinks, and the lessons we paid for. This is context for doing the task well — not a reviewer to please. Every entry carries its *why*; if the why doesn't apply to your situation, reasoning from first principles beats rule-following.
4	
5	Companion file: `db-domain-invariants.md` (same directory) — greppable schema/data-layer facts. Read it before touching `packages/database`, any Supabase query, or cross-app contract code.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Working philosophies
10	
11	**Every line is a liability — justify it or delete it.** The most common review comment on our PRs, by far, is a variant of "why is this here?" (defaults nobody hits, props kept through refactors, state vars with one writer and no reader, `?? fallback` on a value that can't be null). The bar: for each line, name the real code path that needs it. "It doesn't hurt" is not a justification; unused code misleads the next reader about what can happen.
12	
13	**Reuse before writing — and actually search, don't recall.** The single largest class of review feedback (16+ comments in 4 months) is "we already have this": utils, shared components, generated types, markers, constants. Memory of the codebase is unreliable; a 10-second grep is not. Before writing any new function/type/component/constant: grep `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`, and nearby files for the operation or shape. Two slightly-different versions of the same thing is the worst outcome — worse than either version alone.
14	
15	**The data model outlives the feature.** If the data shape is wrong, every feature built on it inherits the wrongness — so contracts (identifiers, nullability, required-vs-optional, ownership) get decided deliberately, not by accident of the first implementation. For any schema or contract change, trace what happens to *existing* data: orphaned rows, half-migrated states, rows created by the other app. The clean-new-data path is easy; messy-existing-data is where bugs live.
16	
17	**Separate pure logic from I/O from platform.** Pure transforms are testable and reusable across apps (this is why shared logic lives in `packages/database/src/lib`); I/O wrappers hold integration concerns; platform-specific branching (`"Roam"`/`"Obsidian"`) is passed in as input, never hard-coded inside generic functions.
18	
19	**Scope is a contract.** A PR titled X contains X — every hunk maps to the ticket. Out-of-scope discoveries become Linear tickets or TODOs with context (`// TODO(ENG-XXXX): … because …`), not opportunistic edits. Shared refactors that stacked PRs depend on go in their own base PR. Deferrals are stated in the PR, not left for the reviewer to discover.
20	
21	**Prove it works by driving it.** Green unit tests don't demonstrate UI flows, multi-user behavior, or load-order effects. User-facing changes get a runtime demo (Loom) exercising the real flow; controls must initialize from persisted state, not just react to clicks. (The `/demo-handoff` skill covers how to demo stacked/parallel work.)
22	
23	**Cross-app alignment beats local invention.** Roam↔Obsidian features share contracts. Before designing a Roam-side shape or UX, check how Obsidian already does it; match it or explicitly flag the divergence to the feature owner. "We found it easier in Obsidian to…" is a recurring, and usually correct, review response.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Hard-learned lessons (with sources)
28	
29	### Frontend (Roam plugin, website)
30	
31	- **Tailwind on the predefined scale only.** No inline CSS, no arbitrary values (`h-[37px]`, `text-[15px]`), no hardcoded colors, no component-local `styles.css`. Why: consistent definitions are the point of Tailwind; arbitrary values fork the design system silently. Arbitrary values only when load-bearing (e.g. Radix CSS vars). (PR #958 and 6 others)
32	- **Hoist repeated/typo-prone string literals to named constants.** Selectors, prop keys, attribute names: define once, reference everywhere. Why: `"setting"` vs `"settings"` typos fail silently at runtime. (PR #1067 and 5 others)
33	- **Use current Roam APIs:** `ui.react.Block` to render blocks; `data.async.fast.q` / `data.async.q` for reads. Never sync `.q`; avoid `async.backend` (flaky). Why: sync/legacy paths block the main thread or intermittently fail. (4 PRs)
34	- **Settings persist to Roam block props** (the canonical store) and must preserve the `isNewSettingsStoreEnabled` gate/migration state the old accessors enforced. Bypassing an accessor silently forks the store. (4 PRs)
35	- **Names state exactly what they hold or do.** `setSearchTerm`, not `setSearch`; `initialLoad`, not `loaded`; UI labels specific enough that a user knows what happens. Why: a name the reader guesses wrong about is a bug vector. (PR #1214 and 6 others)
36	- **Domain vocabulary is reserved.** "Candidate" means *Candidate Nodes* in DG (likely a future DB concept) — don't use it for anything else in types/variables/functions. Before naming a cross-app concept, check what the sibling app already calls it and prefer that name (Obsidian's `publishedNodes` beat Roam-side `candidates`). Why: a name that collides with a domain term will be renamed in review; a name that diverges from the sibling app doubles the vocabulary. (PR #1216)
37	- **Type assertions are a last resort.** No `as`, `any`, `unknown`-and-cast for external APIs; narrow with type guards or fix the type at its source (add missing types to roamjs-components rather than casting around them). Same for `!`: "Avoid `!` whenever possible. If not possible, add a comment explaining why" (mdroidian, PRs #1329/#1324). For untyped third-party surfaces, maintain our own minimal `unofficial-types.ts` with only the types we need — don't add unofficial community typings packages to package.json (PR #1271). Why: assertions turn compile-time errors into runtime surprises. (6 PRs)
38	- **New UI is feature-gated.** If the parent feature has a flag, the new element checks it. "If we merge this, is it ready for Pilot Users?" must have an answer.
39	- **Prefer platform-native APIs: `window.roamAlphaAPI` > roamjs-components > hand-rolled.** The typed surface is not the full runtime surface — roamjs-components' types lag Roam's actual API (e.g. `data.page.fromMarkdown` / `data.block.fromMarkdown` exist but are untyped; declare locally and cast). Before concluding a capability doesn't exist, check `roam-api-surface.md` in this directory (regenerate per its instructions). Why: two independent ENG-1858 implementations diverged on exactly this — one hand-rolled a markdown parser the platform already ships. (ENG-1858, 2026-07; preference order set by sid.)
40	- **Helpers wrapping a `roamAlphaAPI` write must surface the promise.** A success-reporting path that fires-and-forgets a write claims success it can't know; a floating promise inside a shared helper (`setBlockProps` pre-ENG-1858) makes every caller unable to await. Fix the helper (return the promise), `void` the call sites that genuinely don't care. (ENG-1858)
41	- **New comments are load-bearing or absent.** A comment that restates the code or narrates the change is noise — mdroidian's literal words, twice: "Claude, chill on the comments" (PRs #1222, #1321; also #1292, #1284). A comment must be parseable by a cold reader from the file alone; one that references off-file context draws "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" instead of understanding. Why: agents over-comment by default, and every unclear comment is a review round-trip.
42	- **Persisted data stores stable IDs, never display names.** Names ("frameName") are subject to change and belong only in the UI at choosing time; saved data references by stable id (`frameShapeId`, uid). Why: name-keyed lookups silently break on rename. (PR #1222)
43	- **Look up settings-tree children by key, never by position.** `tree[3]` compiles, matches the tree you just built, and writes markdown into the wrong parent the moment someone reorders a setting; use `getSubTree({ tree, key: "Template" })`. (PR #1302)
44	- **`Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary.** Excluded from user-selectable type lists (PR #1298, #1272); a remote schema is never resolved to a built-in solely by name, and a configured type never takes a reserved name — mapping a remote "Block" schema to the local built-in silently discards its identity, format, and semantics. #1331 was blocked on exactly this. For v0, block the names and ticket proper conflict resolution.
45	- **User-facing copy speaks user vocabulary; internal operations are silent.** A toast saying "backfilled" means nothing to a user — internal bookkeeping (backfills, migrations, sync housekeeping) reports to PostHog only. # Engineering Context — discourse-graph

What you need to know to do good work in this codebase: how the team thinks, and the lessons we paid for. This is context for doing the task well — not a reviewer to please. Every entry carries its *why*; if the why doesn't apply to your situation, reasoning from first principles beats rule-following.

Companion file: `db-domain-invariants.md` (same directory) — greppable schema/data-layer facts. Read it before touching `packages/database`, any Supabase query, or cross-app contract code.

---

## Working philosophies

**Every line is a liability — justify it or delete it.** The most common review comment on our PRs, by far, is a variant of "why is this here?" (defaults nobody hits, props kept through refactors, state vars with one writer and no reader, `?? fallback` on a value that can't be null). The bar: for each line, name the real code path that needs it. "It doesn't hurt" is not a justification; unused code misleads the next reader about what can happen.

**Reuse before writing — and actually search, don't recall.** The single largest class of review feedback (16+ comments in 4 months) is "we already have this": utils, shared components, generated types, markers, constants. Memory of the codebase is unreliable; a 10-second grep is not. Before writing any new function/type/component/constant: grep `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`, and nearby files for the operation or shape. Two slightly-different versions of the same thing is the worst outcome — worse than either version alone.

**The data model outlives the feature.** If the data shape is wrong, every feature built on it inherits the wrongness — so contracts (identifiers, nullability, required-vs-optional, ownership) get decided deliberately, not by accident of the first implementation. For any schema or contract change, trace what happens to *existing* data: orphaned rows, half-migrated states, rows created by the other app. The clean-new-data path is easy; messy-existing-data is where bugs live.

**Separate pure logic from I/O from platform.** Pure transforms are testable and reusable across apps (this is why shared logic lives in `packages/database/src/lib`); I/O wrappers hold integration concerns; platform-specific branching (`"Roam"`/`"Obsidian"`) is passed in as input, never hard-coded inside generic functions.

**Scope is a contract.** A PR titled X contains X — every hunk maps to the ticket. Out-of-scope discoveries become Linear tickets or TODOs with context (`// TODO(ENG-XXXX): … because …`), not opportunistic edits. Shared refactors that stacked PRs depend on go in their own base PR. Deferrals are stated in the PR, not left for the reviewer to discover.

**Prove it works by driving it.** Green unit tests don't demonstrate UI flows, multi-user behavior, or load-order effects. User-facing changes get a runtime demo (Loom) exercising the real flow; controls must initialize from persisted state, not just react to clicks. (The `/demo-handoff` skill covers how to demo stacked/parallel work.)

**Cross-app alignment beats local invention.** Roam↔Obsidian features share contracts. Before designing a Roam-side shape or UX, check how Obsidian already does it; match it or explicitly flag the divergence to the feature owner. "We found it easier in Obsidian to…" is a recurring, and usually correct, review response.

---

## Hard-learned lessons (with sources)

### Frontend (Roam plugin, website)

- **Tailwind on the predefined scale only.** No inline CSS, no arbitrary values (`h-[37px]`, `text-[15px]`), no hardcoded colors, no component-local `styles.css`. Why: consistent definitions are the point of Tailwind; arbitrary values fork the design system silently. Arbitrary values only when load-bearing (e.g. Radix CSS vars). (PR #958 and 6 others)
- **Hoist repeated/typo-prone string literals to named constants.** Selectors, prop keys, attribute names: define once, reference everywhere. Why: `"setting"` vs `"settings"` typos fail silently at runtime. (PR #1067 and 5 others)
- **Use current Roam APIs:** `ui.react.Block` to render blocks; `data.async.fast.q` / `data.async.q` for reads. Never sync `.q`; avoid `async.backend` (flaky). Why: sync/legacy paths block the main thread or intermittently fail. (4 PRs)
- **Settings persist to Roam block props** (the canonical store) and must preserve the `isNewSettingsStoreEnabled` gate/migration state the old accessors enforced. Bypassing an accessor silently forks the store. (4 PRs)
- **Names state exactly what they hold or do.** `setSearchTerm`, not `setSearch`; `initialLoad`, not `loaded`; UI labels specific enough that a user knows what happens. Why: a name the reader guesses wrong about is a bug vector. (PR #1214 and 6 others)
- **Domain vocabulary is reserved.** "Candidate" means *Candidate Nodes* in DG (likely a future DB concept) — don't use it for anything else in types/variables/functions. Before naming a cross-app concept, check what the sibling app already calls it and prefer that name (Obsidian's `publishedNodes` beat Roam-side `candidates`). Why: a name that collides with a domain term will be renamed in review; a name that diverges from the sibling app doubles the vocabulary. (PR #1216)
- **Type assertions are a last resort.** No `as`, `any`, `unknown`-and-cast for external APIs; narrow with type guards or fix the type at its source (add missing types to roamjs-components rather than casting around them). Same for `!`: "Avoid `!` whenever possible. If not possible, add a comment explaining why" (mdroidian, PRs #1329/#1324). For untyped third-party surfaces, maintain our own minimal `unofficial-types.ts` with only the types we need — don't add unofficial community typings packages to package.json (PR #1271). Why: assertions turn compile-time errors into runtime surprises. (6 PRs)
- **New UI is feature-gated.** If the parent feature has a flag, the new element checks it. "If we merge this, is it ready for Pilot Users?" must have an answer.
- **Prefer platform-native APIs: `window.roamAlphaAPI` > roamjs-components > hand-rolled.** The typed surface is not the full runtime surface — roamjs-components' types lag Roam's actual API (e.g. `data.page.fromMarkdown` / `data.block.fromMarkdown` exist but are untyped; declare locally and cast). Before concluding a capability doesn't exist, check `roam-api-surface.md` in this directory (regenerate per its instructions). Why: two independent ENG-1858 implementations diverged on exactly this — one hand-rolled a markdown parser the platform already ships. (ENG-1858, 2026-07; preference order set by sid.)
- **Helpers wrapping a `roamAlphaAPI` write must surface the promise.** A success-reporting path that fires-and-forgets a write claims success it can't know; a floating promise inside a shared helper (`setBlockProps` pre-ENG-1858) makes every caller unable to await. - **New comments are load-bearing or absent.** A comment that restates the code or narrates the change is noise — mdroidian's literal words, twice: "Claude, chill on the comments" (PRs #1222, #1321; also #1292, #1284). Why: agents over-comment by default, and every unclear comment is a review round-trip.
- **Persisted data stores stable IDs, never display names.** Names ("frameName") are subject to change and belong only in the UI at choosing time; saved data references by stable id (`frameShapeId`, uid). Why: name-keyed lookups silently break on rename. (PR #1222)
- **Look up settings-tree children by key, never by position.** `tree[3]` compiles, matches the tree you just built, and writes markdown into the wrong parent the moment someone reorders a setting; use `getSubTree({ tree, key: "Template" })`. (PR #1302)
- **`Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary.** Excluded from user-selectable type lists (PR #1298, #1272); a remote schema is never resolved to a built-in solely by name, and a configured type never takes a reserved name — mapping a remote "Block" schema to the local built-in silently discards its identity, format, and semantics. #1331 was blocked on exactly this. For v0, block the names and ticket proper conflict resolution.
- **User-facing copy speaks user vocabulary; internal operations are silent.** A toast saying "backfilled" means nothing to a user — internal bookkeeping (backfills, migrations, sync housekeeping) reports to PostHog only. 1	# Data-Layer Invariants — discourse-graph
2	
3	Facts about our schema and data layer that code must respect. Each entry: the invariant, the check to run against a diff, and the source of truth in the repo. This file is DATA, not prose — keep entries short, greppable, and current.
4	
5	**Feedback loop:** when a reviewer comment reveals an invariant not listed here, append it (invariant → check → source → the PR where we learned it). When the schema changes, update the affected entry. This file is the single home for schema facts; review skills read it at runtime.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Concept table
10	
11	- **Node queries filter on `is_relation = false`, not `arity`.** Since migration `20260819023727_is_relation_column` (on origin/main from 2026-08-19) `Concept` carries two derived columns: `arity` (`compute_arity_local`, the role count) and `is_relation` (`compute_is_relation_local`, true when the schema's `literal_content.roles` is `["source","destination"]`). Every node-listing chain on main uses `.eq("is_relation", false)`; `.eq("arity", 0)` is the pre-migration form and only survives on branches cut before 2026-08-19 (e.g. the #1317/#1318/#1332 stack), where it must be switched on rebase. The two are not equivalent for a schema with a non-standard role set, so do not mix them.
12	  Check: every `.from("my_concepts")`/`.from("Concept")` chain in the diff that means "nodes" has the `is_relation` filter (or `arity` only on a pre-migration base, with the rebase switch named in the PR).
13	  Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql` (`compute_is_relation_local`, `is_relation` column). Learned: PR #1147, #1214; updated 2026-08-23 after the #1330/#1332 reviews.
14	
15	- **`is_schema = true` rows are node-type schemas, not instances.** Instance queries filter `.eq("is_schema", false)`; a typed instance also has `schema_id != null`.
16	  Source: `concept.sql`.
17	
18	## Timestamps
19	
20	- **All `created`/`last_modified` columns are `timestamp without time zone` holding naive UTC.** PostgREST returns them with **no `Z` suffix**, so `Date.parse(x)` / `new Date(x)` parses them as *local* time — a correctness bug (display shift, wrong sort around DST, and writing invalid data back). Parse as explicit UTC (append `Z`), normalize to `toISOString()` before compare/sort/display, write only canonical UTC. Test fixtures must use the production shape (Z-less).
21	  Check: every timestamp value read from a PostgREST response in the diff is normalized before use; no naive `Date.parse` on DB values.
22	  Source: `concept.sql`, `content.sql` (`timestamp without time zone`). Learned: PR #1214 ("For me UTC is a blocker — it means inserting invalid data"). Repo-wide cleanup: ENG-2034.
23	  Note: values already normalized (e.g. by `packages/database` helpers returning `toISOString()`) must NOT get another `Z` appended — trace which side of the boundary you're on.
24	
25	## Generated types
26	
27	- **Enums and table row types already exist in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`** (`Enums<"Platform">`, `Tables<"my_contents">`, …). Never hand-write an inline union or interface whose shape duplicates a generated one.
28	  Check: for every inline string-literal union in the diff (pattern `"X" | "Y"`), grep its members in `dbTypes.ts`; if they match an enum, use `Enums<"…">`.
29	  Source: `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts` (generated). Learned: PR #1214.
30	  Import as `@repo/database/dbTypes` from apps (not relative paths).
31	
32	## Queries (PostgREST / Supabase)
33	
34	- **Push predicates into the request.** Filtering/sorting/slicing that PostgREST can do (`.eq`, `.neq`, `.in`, `.order`, `.limit`) must not be done in client JS after fetching.
35	  Check: any `.filter(...)`/`.find(...)`/sort on rows straight from a response → could the query express it?
36	  Learned: PR #1214 (client-side `space_id !== currentSpaceId`), #1147.
37	
38	- **Offset pagination needs a fully unique ORDER BY.** With `.range()` over non-unique order keys, tied rows can duplicate or vanish across page boundaries. Add a tiebreaker column so the total ordering is unique.
39	  Check: every paginated query's `.order()` chain uniquely identifies rows.
40	  Learned: PR #1214.
41	
42	- **List/discovery queries never select heavy payload columns.** `text` (full variant), `literal_content`, etc. are import-time data; discovery/listing selects summaries only. Defer content fetch until the user acts.
43	  Check: `.select()` column lists in listing paths contain no payload columns.
44	  Learned: PR #1214 (mdroidian's top concern).
45	
46	- **Don't hit the DB inside a per-item loop.** Gather inputs, then one batched query (`.in(...)`, chunked if needed).
47	  Learned: PR #847.
48	
49	- **An empty result under RLS is ambiguous.** "Row doesn't exist" and "row not visible to this client/role" look identical. When emptiness drives a decision (create-vs-skip, error message), account for visibility.
50	  Learned: PR #510.
51	
52	- **Content queries expecting one row per (space, node, variant) must filter `original = true`.** Non-original (derived) rows carry `original = NULL` ("Use null, never false" — `content.sql`), so only `(space_id, source_local_id, variant, original)` is unique; a bare variant filter + `maybeSingle()` errors the moment a derived representation exists.
53	  Check: every `.maybeSingle()` on `Content`/`my_contents` filtered by variant also filters `original`.
54	  Source: `content.sql` (original column + unique indexes). Learned: Codex review on PR #1267 (ENG-1858); Obsidian's `fetchNodeContent`/`fetchNodeContentForImport` still carry the latent issue.
55	
56	## Cross-app contract
57	
58	- **Identity is the RID; don't carry decomposed duplicates.** Store/pass `rid` and derive space/node/app via `packages/database/src/lib/rid.ts` utils (`spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`, `isRid`). A struct holding both a RID and its decomposed parts is redundant modelling.
59	  Check: new types carrying `rid` + `sourceSpaceId`/`sourceApp`/`sourceNodeId` together need a reason.
60	  Learned: PR #1161. Direction (maparent): converge on `localId` which may itself be a RID — preserve RID-shaped local IDs (`isRid`: `https://` or `orn:` prefix) instead of re-deriving.
61	
62	- **`direct` and `full` content variants are disjoint: title vs body.** `direct` = title/label; `full` = body, and per ENG-2016 `full` is **optional**. Don't assume every shared node has `full`; don't concatenate title into body.
63	  Learned: PR #1147, ENG-2016.
64	
65	- **Schema contracts live in `packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`** (ENG-1984). Extend contracts there, not with app-local shapes. New exported types in `packages/database/src/lib` that describe cross-app data must reuse/extend a contract type or state in the PR why they don't.
66	  Learned: PR #1216 ("Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?").
67	
68	- **Inputs crossing the app boundary are validated at entry.** Before consuming another app's data: `isRid` on RIDs (never a prefix test — `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid` also emits `https://`-shaped RIDs), timestamp parseability (canonicalize with `toISOString()`), and `content_type` against `contentTypes.*` from `@repo/content-model` before using `full` text (Roam-produced `text/markdown` embeds the title as an H1; Obsidian emits `text/obsidian+markdown`).
69	  Check: new cross-app consumers validate before writing locally.
70	  Learned: ENG-1858 (v2/v3 delta — one implementation validated, one didn't).
71	
72	- **Pure text/markdown transforms shared across apps live in `@repo/content-model`** (`text` module: `normalizeLineEndings`, `stripFrontmatter`) — not app-local copies. Obsidian's `full` variant is the raw note file including YAML frontmatter; consumers strip it via the shared helper.
73	  Check: any new pure text transform in an app has a reason not to live in content-model.
74	  Learned: ENG-1858.
75	
76	- **Obsidian frontmatter is deliberately dual-homed: `literal_content.source_data` (jsonb, indexed, key order lost) AND the `full` body (lossless).** The producer does not strip it; consumers strip at use (MVP0). Consumer-side stripping is acknowledged debt to revisit at the atJSON transfer, where strippable regions get marked platform-agnostically so no platform needs to know another's specifics.
77	  Check: don't propose producer-side stripping or remove the body copy; don't parse frontmatter fields out of `full` text — structured reads come from `source_data`.
78	  Source: maparent on PR #1224 (2026-07). Future: frontmatter → Roam props translation is unticketed future scope, sourced from `source_data`, not re-parsed text.
79	
80	- **Platform can in principle be derived from a RID** — maparent proposes augmenting `ridToSpaceUriAndLocalId` to return `Platform`. Until that lands, `my_spaces.platform` is the source of truth when a Space row is in hand; flows starting from a stored RID alone (refresh, ENG-1860) resolve via `getSpaceNameIdFromRid`.
81	  Source: maparent on PR #1224 (2026-07), open offer.
82	
83	- **A field added/renamed on a contract or schema type is handled in every converter, both directions.** The converter surface: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp, since ENG-2146), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` (Roam→CrossApp), and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side).
84	  Check: for every field added to a `CrossApp*` type or schema `literal_content`, grep each converter file; every miss is either handled or named as deferred with a ticket in the PR.
85	  Learned: PR #1316, #1317 (maparent: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions").
86	
87	- **Contract-extracted values take precedence over raw `source_data`.** Where a value exists both parsed-from-contract and in `source_data` (e.g. node type `format`), the contract-side value wins — `source_data` stays unprocessed and diverges once we modify values; Obsidian's `parseSchemaLiteralContent` should converge on the same precedence. `format` being stored in two places is an open decision — Roam decision page `eFt8yo8Zq` — check it before touching format storage.
88	  Source: maparent + mdroidian on PR #1331 (2026-08, open).
89	
90	## Sync gating
91	
92	- **Sync flag off ⇒ no DB communication.** A user who turned sync off expects zero DB traffic; a maintenance write behind that expectation (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out and sign-off in the PR ("with alpha only users, we can push this change through" — a one-time pass, not a precedent). Internal outcomes ("backfilled N nodes") report to PostHog only — never a user toast; "backfilled" is not user vocabulary.
93	  Check: every new DB write path names the user-visible flag/action that authorizes it; no toasts for internal bookkeeping.
94	  Learned: PR #1332 (mdroidian, 2026-08).
95	
96	## Datalog (Roam queries)
97	
98	- **Bind page vs block facts explicitly.** A query separating page-level and block-level values (e.g. edit times) must bind both `?page` and `?node` (`[?node :block/page ?page]`) — binding only `?node` silently collapses the two.
99	  Learned: PR #1147.
100	
101	## Telemetry & errors
102	
103	- **Caught errors report to PostHog, not `console.error`.** Any failure affecting a user action also gets a user-facing message (toast/alert). `console.error` is invisible to both users and us.
104	  Learned: PR #1214, ENG-1092.
105	
106	## Schema files & migrations
107	
108	- **`DROP` statements belong in migrations, not schema files.** Schemas describe the target state; migrations move between states, ideally idempotent and incremental (only re-process what changed).
109	  Learned: PR #315, #748.

# Data-Layer Invariants — discourse-graph

Facts about our schema and data layer that code must respect. Each entry: the invariant, the check to run against a diff, and the source of truth in the repo. This file is DATA, not prose — keep entries short, greppable, and current.

**Feedback loop:** when a reviewer comment reveals an invariant not listed here, append it (invariant → check → source → the PR where we learned it). When the schema changes, update the affected entry. This file is the single home for schema facts; review skills read it at runtime.

---

## Concept table

- **Node queries filter on `is_relation = false`, not `arity`.** Since migration `20260819023727_is_relation_column` (on origin/main from 2026-08-19) `Concept` carries two derived columns: `arity` (`compute_arity_local`, the role count) and `is_relation` (`compute_is_relation_local`, true when the schema's `literal_content.roles` is `["source","destination"]`). Every node-listing chain on main uses `.eq("is_relation", false)`; `.eq("arity", 0)` is the pre-migration form and only survives on branches cut before 2026-08-19 (e.g. the #1317/#1318/#1332 stack), where it must be switched on rebase. The two are not equivalent for a schema with a non-standard role set, so do not mix them.
  Check: every `.from("my_concepts")`/`.from("Concept")` chain in the diff that means "nodes" has the `is_relation` filter (or `arity` only on a pre-migration base, with the rebase switch named in the PR).
  Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql` (`compute_is_relation_local`, `is_relation` column). Learned: PR #1147, #1214; updated 2026-08-23 after the #1330/#1332 reviews.

- **`is_schema = true` rows are node-type schemas, not instances.** Instance queries filter `.eq("is_schema", false)`; a typed instance also has `schema_id != null`.
  Source: `concept.sql`.

## Timestamps

- **All `created`/`last_modified` columns are `timestamp without time zone` holding naive UTC.** PostgREST returns them with **no `Z` suffix**, so `Date.parse(x)` / `new Date(x)` parses them as *local* time — a correctness bug (display shift, wrong sort around DST, and writing invalid data back). Parse as explicit UTC (append `Z`), normalize to `toISOString()` before compare/sort/display, write only canonical UTC. Test fixtures must use the production shape (Z-less).
  Check: every timestamp value read from a PostgREST response in the diff is normalized before use; no naive `Date.parse` on DB values.
  Source: `concept.sql`, `content.sql` (`timestamp without time zone`). Learned: PR #1214 ("For me UTC is a blocker — it means inserting invalid data"). Repo-wide cleanup: ENG-2034.
  Note: values already normalized (e.g. by `packages/database` helpers returning `toISOString()`) must NOT get another `Z` appended — trace which side of the boundary you're on.

## Generated types

- **Enums and table row types already exist in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`** (`Enums<"Platform">`, `Tables<"my_contents">`, …). Never hand-write an inline union or interface whose shape duplicates a generated one.
  Check: for every inline string-literal union in the diff (pattern `"X" | "Y"`), grep its members in `dbTypes.ts`; if they match an enum, use `Enums<"…">`.
  Source: `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts` (generated). Learned: PR #1214.
  Import as `@repo/database/dbTypes` from apps (not relative paths).

## Queries (PostgREST / Supabase)

- **Push predicates into the request.** Filtering/sorting/slicing that PostgREST can do (`.eq`, `.neq`, `.in`, `.order`, `.limit`) must not be done in client JS after fetching.
  Check: any `.filter(...)`/`.find(...)`/sort on rows straight from a response → could the query express it?
  Learned: PR #1214 (client-side `space_id !== currentSpaceId`), #1147.

- **Offset pagination needs a fully unique ORDER BY.** With `.range()` over non-unique order keys, tied rows can duplicate or vanish across page boundaries. Add a tiebreaker column so the total ordering is unique.
  Check: every paginated query's `.order()` chain uniquely identifies rows.
  Learned: PR #1214.

- **List/discovery queries never select heavy payload columns.** `text` (full variant), `literal_content`, etc. are import-time data; discovery/listing selects summaries only. Defer content fetch until the user acts.
  Check: `.select()` column lists in listing paths contain no payload columns.
  Learned: PR #1214 (mdroidian's top concern).

- **Don't hit the DB inside a per-item loop.** Gather inputs, then one batched query (`.in(...)`, chunked if needed).
  Learned: PR #847.

- **An empty result under RLS is ambiguous.** "Row doesn't exist" and "row not visible to this client/role" look identical. When emptiness drives a decision (create-vs-skip, error message), account for visibility.
  Learned: PR #510.

- **Content queries expecting one row per (space, node, variant) must filter `original = true`.** Non-original (derived) rows carry `original = NULL` ("Use null, never false" — `content.sql`), so only `(space_id, source_local_id, variant, original)` is unique; a bare variant filter + `maybeSingle()` errors the moment a derived representation exists.
  Check: every `.maybeSingle()` on `Content`/`my_contents` filtered by variant also filters `original`.
  Source: `content.sql` (original column + unique indexes). Learned: Codex review on PR #1267 (ENG-1858); Obsidian's `fetchNodeContent`/`fetchNodeContentForImport` still carry the latent issue.

## Cross-app contract

- **Identity is the RID; don't carry decomposed duplicates.** Store/pass `rid` and derive space/node/app via `packages/database/src/lib/rid.ts` utils (`spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`, `isRid`). A struct holding both a RID and its decomposed parts is redundant modelling.
  Check: new types carrying `rid` + `sourceSpaceId`/`sourceApp`/`sourceNodeId` together need a reason.
  Learned: PR #1161. Direction (maparent): converge on `localId` which may itself be a RID — preserve RID-shaped local IDs (`isRid`: `https://` or `orn:` prefix) instead of re-deriving.

- **`direct` and `full` content variants are disjoint: title vs body.** `direct` = title/label; `full` = body, and per ENG-2016 `full` is **optional**. Don't assume every shared node has `full`; don't concatenate title into body.
  Learned: PR #1147, ENG-2016.

- **Schema contracts live in `packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`** (ENG-1984). Extend contracts there, not with app-local shapes. New exported types in `packages/database/src/lib` that describe cross-app data must reuse/extend a contract type or state in the PR why they don't.
  Learned: PR #1216 ("Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?").

- **Inputs crossing the app boundary are validated at entry.** Before consuming another app's data: `isRid` on RIDs (never a prefix test — `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid` also emits `https://`-shaped RIDs), timestamp parseability (canonicalize with `toISOString()`), and `content_type` against `contentTypes.*` from `@repo/content-model` before using `full` text (Roam-produced `text/markdown` embeds the title as an H1; Obsidian emits `text/obsidian+markdown`).
  Check: new cross-app consumers validate before writing locally.
  Learned: ENG-1858 (v2/v3 delta — one implementation validated, one didn't).

- **Pure text/markdown transforms shared across apps live in `@repo/content-model`** (`text` module: `normalizeLineEndings`, `stripFrontmatter`) — not app-local copies. Obsidian's `full` variant is the raw note file including YAML frontmatter; consumers strip it via the shared helper.
  Check: any new pure text transform in an app has a reason not to live in content-model.
  Learned: ENG-1858.

- **Obsidian frontmatter is deliberately dual-homed: `literal_content.source_data` (jsonb, indexed, key order lost) AND the `full` body (lossless).** The producer does not strip it; consumers strip at use (MVP0). Consumer-side stripping is acknowledged debt to revisit at the atJSON transfer, where strippable regions get marked platform-agnostically so no platform needs to know another's specifics.
  Check: don't propose producer-side stripping or remove the body copy; don't parse frontmatter fields out of `full` text — structured reads come from `source_data`.
  Source: maparent on PR #1224 (2026-07). Future: frontmatter → Roam props translation is unticketed future scope, sourced from `source_data`, not re-parsed text.

- **Platform can in principle be derived from a RID** — maparent proposes augmenting `ridToSpaceUriAndLocalId` to return `Platform`. Until that lands, `my_spaces.platform` is the source of truth when a Space row is in hand; flows starting from a stored RID alone (refresh, ENG-1860) resolve via `getSpaceNameIdFromRid`.
  Source: maparent on PR #1224 (2026-07), open offer.

- **A field added/renamed on a contract or schema type is handled in every converter, both directions.** The converter surface: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp, since ENG-2146), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` (Roam→CrossApp), and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side).
  Check: for every field added to a `CrossApp*` type or schema `literal_content`, grep each converter file; every miss is either handled or named as deferred with a ticket in the PR.
  Learned: PR #1316, #1317 (maparent: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions").

- **Contract-extracted values take precedence over raw `source_data`.** Where a value exists both parsed-from-contract and in `source_data` (e.g. node type `format`), the contract-side value wins — `source_data` stays unprocessed and diverges once we modify values; Obsidian's `parseSchemaLiteralContent` should converge on the same precedence. `format` being stored in two places is an open decision — Roam decision page `eFt8yo8Zq` — check it before touching format storage.
  Source: maparent + mdroidian on PR #1331 (2026-08, open).

## Sync gating

- **Sync flag off ⇒ no DB communication.** A user who turned sync off expects zero DB traffic; a maintenance write behind that expectation (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out and sign-off in the PR ("with alpha only users, we can push this change through" — a one-time pass, not a precedent). Internal outcomes ("backfilled N nodes") report to PostHog only — never a user toast; "backfilled" is not user vocabulary.
  Check: every new DB write path names the user-visible flag/action that authorizes it; no toasts for internal bookkeeping.
  Learned: PR #1332 (mdroidian, 2026-08).

## Datalog (Roam queries)

- **Bind page vs block facts explicitly.** A query separating page-level and block-level values (e.g. edit times) must bind both `?page` and `?node` (`[?node :block/page ?page]`) — binding only `?node` silently collapses the two.
  Learned: PR #1147.

## Telemetry & errors

- **Caught errors report to PostHog, not `console.error`.** Any failure affecting a user action also gets a user-facing message (toast/alert). `console.error` is invisible to both users and us.
  Learned: PR #1214, ENG-1092.

## Schema files & migrations

- **`DROP` statements belong in migrations, not schema files.** Schemas describe the target state; migrations move between states, ideally idempotent and incremental (only re-process what changed).
  Learned: PR #315, #748.

1	# Engineering Context — discourse-graph
2	
3	What you need to know to do good work in this codebase: how the team thinks, and the lessons we paid for. This is context for doing the task well — not a reviewer to please. Every entry carries its *why*; if the why doesn't apply to your situation, reasoning from first principles beats rule-following.
4	
5	Companion file: `db-domain-invariants.md` (same directory) — greppable schema/data-layer facts. Read it before touching `packages/database`, any Supabase query, or cross-app contract code.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Working philosophies
10	
11	**Every line is a liability — justify it or delete it.** The most common review comment on our PRs, by far, is a variant of "why is this here?" (defaults nobody hits, props kept through refactors, state vars with one writer and no reader, `?? fallback` on a value that can't be null). The bar: for each line, name the real code path that needs it. "It doesn't hurt" is not a justification; unused code misleads the next reader about what can happen.
12	
13	**Reuse before writing — and actually search, don't recall.** The single largest class of review feedback (16+ comments in 4 months) is "we already have this": utils, shared components, generated types, markers, constants. Memory of the codebase is unreliable; a 10-second grep is not. Before writing any new function/type/component/constant: grep `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`, and nearby files for the operation or shape. Two slightly-different versions of the same thing is the worst outcome — worse than either version alone.
14	
15	**The data model outlives the feature.** If the data shape is wrong, every feature built on it inherits the wrongness — so contracts (identifiers, nullability, required-vs-optional, ownership) get decided deliberately, not by accident of the first implementation. For any schema or contract change, trace what happens to *existing* data: orphaned rows, half-migrated states, rows created by the other app. The clean-new-data path is easy; messy-existing-data is where bugs live.
16	
17	**Separate pure logic from I/O from platform.** Pure transforms are testable and reusable across apps (this is why shared logic lives in `packages/database/src/lib`); I/O wrappers hold integration concerns; platform-specific branching (`"Roam"`/`"Obsidian"`) is passed in as input, never hard-coded inside generic functions.
18	
19	**Scope is a contract.** A PR titled X contains X — every hunk maps to the ticket. Out-of-scope discoveries become Linear tickets or TODOs with context (`// TODO(ENG-XXXX): … because …`), not opportunistic edits. Shared refactors that stacked PRs depend on go in their own base PR. Deferrals are stated in the PR, not left for the reviewer to discover.
20	
21	**Prove it works by driving it.** Green unit tests don't demonstrate UI flows, multi-user behavior, or load-order effects. User-facing changes get a runtime demo (Loom) exercising the real flow; controls must initialize from persisted state, not just react to clicks. (The `/demo-handoff` skill covers how to demo stacked/parallel work.)
22	
23	**Cross-app alignment beats local invention.** Roam↔Obsidian features share contracts. Before designing a Roam-side shape or UX, check how Obsidian already does it; match it or explicitly flag the divergence to the feature owner. "We found it easier in Obsidian to…" is a recurring, and usually correct, review response.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Hard-learned lessons (with sources)
28	
29	### Frontend (Roam plugin, website)
30	
31	- **Tailwind on the predefined scale only.** No inline CSS, no arbitrary values (`h-[37px]`, `text-[15px]`), no hardcoded colors, no component-local `styles.css`. Why: consistent definitions are the point of Tailwind; arbitrary values fork the design system silently. Arbitrary values only when load-bearing (e.g. Radix CSS vars). (PR #958 and 6 others)
32	- **Hoist repeated/typo-prone string literals to named constants.** Selectors, prop keys, attribute names: define once, reference everywhere. Why: `"setting"` vs `"settings"` typos fail silently at runtime. (PR #1067 and 5 others)
33	- **Use current Roam APIs:** `ui.react.Block` to render blocks; `data.async.fast.q` / `data.async.q` for reads. Never sync `.q`; avoid `async.backend` (flaky). Why: sync/legacy paths block the main thread or intermittently fail. (4 PRs)
34	- **Settings persist to Roam block props** (the canonical store) and must preserve the `isNewSettingsStoreEnabled` gate/migration state the old accessors enforced. Bypassing an accessor silently forks the store. (4 PRs)
35	- **Names state exactly what they hold or do.** `setSearchTerm`, not `setSearch`; `initialLoad`, not `loaded`; UI labels specific enough that a user knows what happens. Why: a name the reader guesses wrong about is a bug vector. (PR #1214 and 6 others)
36	- **Domain vocabulary is reserved.** "Candidate" means *Candidate Nodes* in DG (likely a future DB concept) — don't use it for anything else in types/variables/functions. Before naming a cross-app concept, check what the sibling app already calls it and prefer that name (Obsidian's `publishedNodes` beat Roam-side `candidates`). Why: a name that collides with a domain term will be renamed in review; a name that diverges from the sibling app doubles the vocabulary. (PR #1216)
37	- **Type assertions are a last resort.** No `as`, `any`, `unknown`-and-cast for external APIs; narrow with type guards or fix the type at its source (add missing types to roamjs-components rather than casting around them). Same for `!`: "Avoid `!` whenever possible. If not possible, add a comment explaining why" (mdroidian, PRs #1329/#1324). For untyped third-party surfaces, maintain our own minimal `unofficial-types.ts` with only the types we need — don't add unofficial community typings packages to package.json (PR #1271). Why: assertions turn compile-time errors into runtime surprises. (6 PRs)
38	- **New UI is feature-gated.** If the parent feature has a flag, the new element checks it. "If we merge this, is it ready for Pilot Users?" must have an answer.
39	- **Prefer platform-native APIs: `window.roamAlphaAPI` > roamjs-components > hand-rolled.** The typed surface is not the full runtime surface — roamjs-components' types lag Roam's actual API (e.g. `data.page.fromMarkdown` / `data.block.fromMarkdown` exist but are untyped; declare locally and cast). Before concluding a capability doesn't exist, check `roam-api-surface.md` in this directory (regenerate per its instructions). Why: two independent ENG-1858 implementations diverged on exactly this — one hand-rolled a markdown parser the platform already ships. (ENG-1858, 2026-07; preference order set by sid.)
40	- **Helpers wrapping a `roamAlphaAPI` write must surface the promise.** A success-reporting path that fires-and-forgets a write claims success it can't know; a floating promise inside a shared helper (`setBlockProps` pre-ENG-1858) makes every caller unable to await. Fix the helper (return the promise), `void` the call sites that genuinely don't care. (ENG-1858)
41	- **New comments are load-bearing or absent.** A comment that restates the code or narrates the change is noise — mdroidian's literal words, twice: "Claude, chill on the comments" (PRs #1222, #1321; also #1292, #1284). A comment must be parseable by a cold reader from the file alone; one that references off-file context draws "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" instead of understanding. Why: agents over-comment by default, and every unclear comment is a review round-trip.
42	- **Persisted data stores stable IDs, never display names.** Names ("frameName") are subject to change and belong only in the UI at choosing time; saved data references by stable id (`frameShapeId`, uid). Why: name-keyed lookups silently break on rename. (PR #1222)
43	- **Look up settings-tree children by key, never by position.** `tree[3]` compiles, matches the tree you just built, and writes markdown into the wrong parent the moment someone reorders a setting; use `getSubTree({ tree, key: "Template" })`. (PR #1302)
44	- **`Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary.** Excluded from user-selectable type lists (PR #1298, #1272); a remote schema is never resolved to a built-in solely by name, and a configured type never takes a reserved name — mapping a remote "Block" schema to the local built-in silently discards its identity, format, and semantics. #1331 was blocked on exactly this. For v0, block the names and ticket proper conflict resolution.
45	- **User-facing copy speaks user vocabulary; internal operations are silent.** A toast saying "backfilled" means nothing to a user — internal bookkeeping (backfills, migrations, sync housekeeping) reports to PostHog only. The toast rule from #1214 cuts both ways: user-affecting failures get a toast; internal milestones don't. (PR #1332)
46	- **A panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise.** Proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering, spacing — reviewers screenshot-compare against the original and file each delta ("the styling menu is now stretched", "missing the purple highlight"). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* is not no relation *types*). (PRs #1255, #1272)
47	
48	### Data layer & cross-app (see `db-domain-invariants.md` for the full checkable list)
49	
50	- **UTC discipline is a blocker-level concern**: naive timestamps written or compared in local time = invalid data in the DB. (PR #1214)
51	- **Discovery/listing queries fetch summaries, not payloads.** Fetching every node's full text to render a list shipped in #1214 and had to be reworked: listing and importing are different operations with different data needs.
52	- **Query shape is correctness, not style**: missing domain filters (`arity = 0`), unbound datalog vars, and non-unique pagination ordering all produce *wrong results*, silently, at data scale you don't test at. (PRs #1147, #1214)
53	- **Identity: one canonical representation.** Carrying a RID plus its decomposed parts in the same struct means two sources of truth; keep the RID, derive the rest. (PR #1161)
54	- **Values ride the pipeline; don't re-derive them downstream.** Before adding a fetch, map-build, or helper lookup, trace where the input data was constructed — if the value existed there (`schema_id` on `SharedNode`, `format` on `matchingNodeType`), thread the field through the intermediate types instead. Both reviewers flag this independently. (PRs #1266, #1317)
55	- **A field added to a cross-app contract is handled in both translation directions.** Producer-side alone is half the work; maparent asks for the missing converter every time ("This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions"). See the converter-matrix entry in `db-domain-invariants.md`. (PRs #1316, #1317)
56	
57	### Process
58	
59	- **Reviewers review the resulting system, not the diff.** mdroidian traces call graphs: a parameter only one caller passes, a wrapper that now only adds one field, an extraction that isn't 1:1 with the original — all get flagged even when each hunk looks fine alone. Before the PR: read the changed files *as they now are* plus every caller. (PR #1216 — all 8 comments were of this class)
60	- **Extraction/refactor PRs owe a parity accounting.** Every place the replacement is not 1:1 with the original ("text", "modifiedAt" handled differently) is a decision; enumerate them in the PR with the why, or the reviewer asks you to "walk through those decisions" one comment at a time. (PR #1216)
61	- **UI features get reviewed by being used.** For DOM-observer/interaction features, mdroidian drives the real graph across surfaces (main window, sidebar, Kanban, query views) and content shapes (multiline, nested refs, titles) and files every behavioral rough edge — hover reflow, icon palette, cursor style, stale observers. Pre-empt: run that matrix yourself, fix what you find, and record the demo with the mouse cursor visible ("there is no mouse in the video" = re-record). Claiming a bug fixed without re-driving it yourself gets asked: "Did you test it?" (PR #1083)
62	- **Demo videos are signal-dense.** State changes are shown visually (a quick caption/toast marking "before fix" / "on branch"), not carried in narration; narration that states the obvious gets mocked in review ("'Every relation has a source and destination' — this is the definition of a relation, yes, thank you 😑"). (PR #1298)
63	- **One problem per PR, under ~500 lines before tests.** mdroidian's stated bar (#1222). Real drive-by discoveries (a refreshConfigTree bug, a merge-conflict handler) are split to their own tickets — and fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
64	- **Resolve bot comments before requesting human review.** Every codex/graphite/devin comment is fixed, or answered with why-not and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is often "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click the resolve button" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — leaving them open costs a full round-trip.
65	- **A stacked chain owes coverage accounting.** When a feature spans sibling tickets, the union of the tickets must cover both platforms and both data directions — "this only handles Obsidian-origin; where's Roam-origin?" recurred across ENG-1858/1859/2158 (#1267, #1269, #1316). State the gap and which ticket owns it in the PR; "can be separate or together, as long as it's noted" (maparent).
66	- **Removing a guard is a claim — argue it in the PR.** State what cases the check protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread one annotation would have preempted; the thread ended "I accept this argument. Approving."
67	- **Read your own diff hunk-by-hunk before opening the PR.** For each hunk, one sentence: why is this here? Anything you can't explain — incidental agent edits, reorderings, leftover scaffolding — gets reverted. Reviewers' most common question is "why?", and every occurrence is an avoidable round-trip.
68	- **Give the reviewer your context.** Removals: what replaces them? New patterns: why? Temporary code: say it's temporary. The test: could someone who never saw the branch review this from the PR description + diff without asking a question?
69	- **Not everything is catchable pre-PR.** ~11% of review comments come from product/1:1 context only the reviewer has. Don't contort; surface open questions in the PR description instead.
70	- **When a ticket names a mechanism, resolve the literal vs semantic reading before designing.** "Use Roam's markdown import/from-markdown behavior" has a literal reading (call that API) and a semantic one (mirror its behavior in our code). Enumerate both, verify which is feasible (see the API-surface doc), and pick deliberately — two ENG-1858 implementations silently picked opposite readings. (2026-07)
71	- **Multi-step Roam write flows return staged results.** Shape: identity echo + `{ success: true, action } | { success: false, pageUid?, error: { message, stage } }`, with one stage name per step (`validate-input`, `fetch-content`, `title-collision`, `create-page`, `replace-page-content`, `update-page-title`, `write-source-identity`, …). Consumers report per-item outcomes from the stage; failures never drop the identity fields. Canonized from the ENG-1858 materializer so future flows converge instead of inventing shapes.

1	# Data-Layer Invariants — discourse-graph
2	
3	Facts about our schema and data layer that code must respect. Each entry: the invariant, the check to run against a diff, and the source of truth in the repo. This file is DATA, not prose — keep entries short, greppable, and current.
4	
5	**Feedback loop:** when a reviewer comment reveals an invariant not listed here, append it (invariant → check → source → the PR where we learned it). When the schema changes, update the affected entry. This file is the single home for schema facts; review skills read it at runtime.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Concept table
10	
11	- **Node queries filter on `is_relation = false`, not `arity`.** Since migration `20260819023727_is_relation_column` (on origin/main from 2026-08-19) `Concept` carries two derived columns: `arity` (`compute_arity_local`, the role count) and `is_relation` (`compute_is_relation_local`, true when the schema's `literal_content.roles` is `["source","destination"]`). Every node-listing chain on main uses `.eq("is_relation", false)`; `.eq("arity", 0)` is the pre-migration form and only survives on branches cut before 2026-08-19 (e.g. the #1317/#1318/#1332 stack), where it must be switched on rebase. The two are not equivalent for a schema with a non-standard role set, so do not mix them.
12	  Check: every `.from("my_concepts")`/`.from("Concept")` chain in the diff that means "nodes" has the `is_relation` filter (or `arity` only on a pre-migration base, with the rebase switch named in the PR).
13	  Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql` (`compute_is_relation_local`, `is_relation` column). Learned: PR #1147, #1214; updated 2026-08-23 after the #1330/#1332 reviews.
14	
15	- **`is_schema = true` rows are node-type schemas, not instances.** Instance queries filter `.eq("is_schema", false)`; a typed instance also has `schema_id != null`.
16	  Source: `concept.sql`.
17	
18	## Timestamps
19	
20	- **All `created`/`last_modified` columns are `timestamp without time zone` holding naive UTC.** PostgREST returns them with **no `Z` suffix**, so `Date.parse(x)` / `new Date(x)` parses them as *local* time — a correctness bug (display shift, wrong sort around DST, and writing invalid data back). Parse as explicit UTC (append `Z`), normalize to `toISOString()` before compare/sort/display, write only canonical UTC. Test fixtures must use the production shape (Z-less).
21	  Check: every timestamp value read from a PostgREST response in the diff is normalized before use; no naive `Date.parse` on DB values.
22	  Source: `concept.sql`, `content.sql` (`timestamp without time zone`). Learned: PR #1214 ("For me UTC is a blocker — it means inserting invalid data"). Repo-wide cleanup: ENG-2034.
23	  Note: values already normalized (e.g. by `packages/database` helpers returning `toISOString()`) must NOT get another `Z` appended — trace which side of the boundary you're on.
24	
25	## Generated types
26	
27	- **Enums and table row types already exist in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`** (`Enums<"Platform">`, `Tables<"my_contents">`, …). Never hand-write an inline union or interface whose shape duplicates a generated one.
28	  Check: for every inline string-literal union in the diff (pattern `"X" | "Y"`), grep its members in `dbTypes.ts`; if they match an enum, use `Enums<"…">`.
29	  Source: `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts` (generated). Learned: PR #1214.
30	  Import as `@repo/database/dbTypes` from apps (not relative paths).
31	
32	## Queries (PostgREST / Supabase)
33	
34	- **Push predicates into the request.** Filtering/sorting/slicing that PostgREST can do (`.eq`, `.neq`, `.in`, `.order`, `.limit`) must not be done in client JS after fetching.
35	  Check: any `.filter(...)`/`.find(...)`/sort on rows straight from a response → could the query express it?
36	  Learned: PR #1214 (client-side `space_id !== currentSpaceId`), #1147.
37	
38	- **Offset pagination needs a fully unique ORDER BY.** With `.range()` over non-unique order keys, tied rows can duplicate or vanish across page boundaries. Add a tiebreaker column so the total ordering is unique.
39	  Check: every paginated query's `.order()` chain uniquely identifies rows.
40	  Learned: PR #1214.
41	
42	- **List/discovery queries never select heavy payload columns.** `text` (full variant), `literal_content`, etc. are import-time data; discovery/listing selects summaries only. Defer content fetch until the user acts.
43	  Check: `.select()` column lists in listing paths contain no payload columns.
44	  Learned: PR #1214 (mdroidian's top concern).
45	
46	- **Don't hit the DB inside a per-item loop.** Gather inputs, then one batched query (`.in(...)`, chunked if needed).
47	  Learned: PR #847.
48	
49	- **An empty result under RLS is ambiguous.** "Row doesn't exist" and "row not visible to this client/role" look identical. When emptiness drives a decision (create-vs-skip, error message), account for visibility.
50	  Learned: PR #510.
51	
52	- **Content queries expecting one row per (space, node, variant) must filter `original = true`.** Non-original (derived) rows carry `original = NULL` ("Use null, never false" — `content.sql`), so only `(space_id, source_local_id, variant, original)` is unique; a bare variant filter + `maybeSingle()` errors the moment a derived representation exists.
53	  Check: every `.maybeSingle()` on `Content`/`my_contents` filtered by variant also filters `original`.
54	  Source: `content.sql` (original column + unique indexes). Learned: Codex review on PR #1267 (ENG-1858); Obsidian's `fetchNodeContent`/`fetchNodeContentForImport` still carry the latent issue.
55	
56	## Cross-app contract
57	
58	- **Identity is the RID; don't carry decomposed duplicates.** Store/pass `rid` and derive space/node/app via `packages/database/src/lib/rid.ts` utils (`spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`, `isRid`). A struct holding both a RID and its decomposed parts is redundant modelling.
59	  Check: new types carrying `rid` + `sourceSpaceId`/`sourceApp`/`sourceNodeId` together need a reason.
60	  Learned: PR #1161. Direction (maparent): converge on `localId` which may itself be a RID — preserve RID-shaped local IDs (`isRid`: `https://` or `orn:` prefix) instead of re-deriving.
61	
62	- **`direct` and `full` content variants are disjoint: title vs body.** `direct` = title/label; `full` = body, and per ENG-2016 `full` is **optional**. Don't assume every shared node has `full`; don't concatenate title into body.
63	  Learned: PR #1147, ENG-2016.
64	
65	- **Schema contracts live in `packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`** (ENG-1984). Extend contracts there, not with app-local shapes. New exported types in `packages/database/src/lib` that describe cross-app data must reuse/extend a contract type or state in the PR why they don't.
66	  Learned: PR #1216 ("Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?").
67	
68	- **Inputs crossing the app boundary are validated at entry.** Before consuming another app's data: `isRid` on RIDs (never a prefix test — `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid` also emits `https://`-shaped RIDs), timestamp parseability (canonicalize with `toISOString()`), and `content_type` against `contentTypes.*` from `@repo/content-model` before using `full` text (Roam-produced `text/markdown` embeds the title as an H1; Obsidian emits `text/obsidian+markdown`).
69	  Check: new cross-app consumers validate before writing locally.
70	  Learned: ENG-1858 (v2/v3 delta — one implementation validated, one didn't).
71	
72	- **Pure text/markdown transforms shared across apps live in `@repo/content-model`** (`text` module: `normalizeLineEndings`, `stripFrontmatter`) — not app-local copies. Obsidian's `full` variant is the raw note file including YAML frontmatter; consumers strip it via the shared helper.
73	  Check: any new pure text transform in an app has a reason not to live in content-model.
74	  Learned: ENG-1858.
75	
76	- **Obsidian frontmatter is deliberately dual-homed: `literal_content.source_data` (jsonb, indexed, key order lost) AND the `full` body (lossless).** The producer does not strip it; consumers strip at use (MVP0). Consumer-side stripping is acknowledged debt to revisit at the atJSON transfer, where strippable regions get marked platform-agnostically so no platform needs to know another's specifics.
77	  Check: don't propose producer-side stripping or remove the body copy; don't parse frontmatter fields out of `full` text — structured reads come from `source_data`.
78	  Source: maparent on PR #1224 (2026-07). Future: frontmatter → Roam props translation is unticketed future scope, sourced from `source_data`, not re-parsed text.
79	
80	- **Platform can in principle be derived from a RID** — maparent proposes augmenting `ridToSpaceUriAndLocalId` to return `Platform`. Until that lands, `my_spaces.platform` is the source of truth when a Space row is in hand; flows starting from a stored RID alone (refresh, ENG-1860) resolve via `getSpaceNameIdFromRid`.
81	  Source: maparent on PR #1224 (2026-07), open offer.
82	
83	- **A field added/renamed on a contract or schema type is handled in every converter, both directions.** The converter surface: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp, since ENG-2146), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` (Roam→CrossApp), and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side).
84	  Check: for every field added to a `CrossApp*` type or schema `literal_content`, grep each converter file; every miss is either handled or named as deferred with a ticket in the PR.
85	  Learned: PR #1316, #1317 (maparent: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions").
86	
87	- **Contract-extracted values take precedence over raw `source_data`.** Where a value exists both parsed-from-contract and in `source_data` (e.g. node type `format`), the contract-side value wins — `source_data` stays unprocessed and diverges once we modify values; Obsidian's `parseSchemaLiteralContent` should converge on the same precedence. `format` being stored in two places is an open decision — Roam decision page `eFt8yo8Zq` — check it before touching format storage.
88	  Source: maparent + mdroidian on PR #1331 (2026-08, open).
89	
90	## Sync gating
91	
92	- **Sync flag off ⇒ no DB communication.** A user who turned sync off expects zero DB traffic; a maintenance write behind that expectation (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out and sign-off in the PR ("with alpha only users, we can push this change through" — a one-time pass, not a precedent). Internal outcomes ("backfilled N nodes") report to PostHog only — never a user toast; "backfilled" is not user vocabulary.
93	  Check: every new DB write path names the user-visible flag/action that authorizes it; no toasts for internal bookkeeping.
94	  Learned: PR #1332 (mdroidian, 2026-08).
95	
96	## Datalog (Roam queries)
97	
98	- **Bind page vs block facts explicitly.** A query separating page-level and block-level values (e.g. edit times) must bind both `?page` and `?node` (`[?node :block/page ?page]`) — binding only `?node` silently collapses the two.
99	  Learned: PR #1147.
100	
101	## Telemetry & errors
102	
103	- **Caught errors report to PostHog, not `console.error`.** Any failure affecting a user action also gets a user-facing message (toast/alert). `console.error` is invisible to both users and us.
104	  Learned: PR #1214, ENG-1092.
105	
106	## Schema files & migrations
107	
108	- **`DROP` statements belong in migrations, not schema files.** Schemas describe the target state; migrations move between states, ideally idempotent and incremental (only re-process what changed).
109	  Learned: PR #315, #748.
